text:
Wuchipoquámeneash [Narragansett: berries of a sour kind]. A kind of sharp Fruit like a Barbary in tast.

Sasémineash [Narragansett: “very sour berries,” the cranberry] another sharp cooling Fruit growing in fresh Waters all the Winter, Excellent in conserve against Feavers.

citation.display: Roger Williams, from A Key into the Language of America (1643), p. 99; the glosses in brackets follow J. Hammond Trumbull’s notes to the 1866 edition
